answer: Tesla's 2024 10-K attributes the lower automotive profit mainly to lower prices. Automotive sales revenue fell roughly 8%, even though deliveries were nearly flat at about 1.79 million vehicles. The company cited price cuts, incentives, and financing offers, plus a shift toward lower-priced vehicle variants, which cut the average selling price. Per-unit costs also fell, but not by enough to offset the lower prices, and costs tied to ramping the Cybertruck and other new products weighed on margins. Growing regulatory credit revenue and some cost reductions partly offset this. Tesla also took restructuring charges in 2024 and spent more on AI and other development, which hurt overall profit beyond vehicle margins. I'm confident about the general drivers but not certain of the exact figures, so check the MD&A section of the 10-K for precise numbers.
